{{nihongo|'''Matsuo Shrine'''|松尾神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

=== Shrine Grounds ===
[[File:Matsuo-jinja (Kameoka) otaki.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Otaki]]
The shrine grounds are located at the foot of Mount Saburōgatake on the eastern side of the {{ill|Kameoka Basin|ja|亀岡盆地|zh|龜岡盆地|qid=Q11181997}}, and have been selected as one of the “100 Natural Sites of Kameoka.”<ref>[http://www.city.kameoka.kyoto.jp/kankyouhozen/kurashi/kurashi/shizen/100sen/083.html 100 Natural Sites of Kameoka: Matsuo Shrine (Kameoka City website)].</ref>

The main hall was constructed in the 7th year of {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} ({{ill|1498|Q6705|qid=Q6705}}) during the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. It is a one-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684|lt=one-bay nagare-zukuri}} structure with a {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|zh|檜皮葺|qid=Q90373477}} roof, and currently stands inside a protective shelter. This main hall is registered as a cultural property by Kyoto Prefecture. In addition, the water used for purification located on the lower level beneath the main hall is spring water flowing from Mount Saburōgatake, known as “Otaki,” and is said never to have dried up even during severe droughts.
